## Project Overview

This capstone builds an end-to-end MLB analytics system that transforms raw
game and pitch-level data into actionable matchup recommendations for hitters
and pitchers. The project combines automated data collection, PostgreSQL
storage, feature engineering, statistical analysis, and machine learning to
support game preparation and pitch-strategy decisions.

**Role:** Data engineering, analytics, machine learning, reporting, and deployment  
**Project type:** Graduate Data Science Capstone  
**Repository:** [View the GitHub repository](https://github.com/perezamp15-hue/data510-capstone)

## Problem & Research Question

Baseball teams have access to enormous amounts of pitch-level data, but turning
that information into useful game-planning recommendations is difficult. Raw
statistics alone do not always explain how a specific hitter should approach a
specific pitcher or how a pitcher should attack an opposing lineup.

This project asks:

**How can historical pitch-level MLB data be transformed into reproducible,
matchup-specific recommendations for hitters and pitchers?**

The goal is to create a system that helps translate large-scale baseball data
into concise scouting information that can support pre-game preparation and
matchup strategy.

## Data & Data Engineering

The system uses MLB game, roster, schedule, and pitch-level data collected from
public MLB endpoints. The pipeline stores structured information in a PostgreSQL
database and supports both historical backfills and recurring updates.

The data pipeline includes:

- MLB schedule and game metadata
- Team and player information
- Pitch-by-pitch game data
- Pitch velocity, movement, location, count, and outcome information
- Batter, pitcher, and matchup-level historical features

The warehouse contains millions of pitch-level observations, which makes
efficient collection, storage, validation, and feature generation an important
part of the project.

The project uses **Python, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Alembic, and Railway** to
manage the collection and production data workflow.

## Methods

The project combines data engineering, statistical analysis, and machine
learning into a single workflow.

First, automated Python collectors retrieve MLB game and pitch information and
load it into a PostgreSQL database. Feature-building scripts then aggregate
historical performance across pitcher, batter, count, and matchup contexts.

The modeling workflow evaluates historical pitch-selection patterns using
multiple levels of context, including overall pitcher tendencies, pitcher-count
combinations, and matchup history. Predictions are evaluated using accuracy,
top-three accuracy, and log loss.

The reporting layer converts these results into scouting reports that highlight
pitch usage, hitter tendencies, matchup strengths and weaknesses, and recommended
attack strategies.

## Results

The system successfully combines automated data collection, feature generation,
modeling, and reporting into a reproducible end-to-end workflow.

Model evaluation showed that adding pitcher-specific context substantially
improved pitch-selection predictions compared with broader overall or
count-only baselines. The strongest models correctly placed the actual pitch
within their top three predictions for roughly three-quarters of evaluated
pitches.

Example test results included:

| Model | Accuracy | Top-3 Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pitcher + Count | 37.1% | 75.9% |
| Pitcher | 37.0% | 76.3% |
| Count Only | 30.7% | 61.4% |
| Overall Baseline | 30.7% | 60.8% |

These results suggest that pitcher-specific tendencies provide meaningful
predictive information beyond count or league-wide tendencies alone.

## Reproducibility

The project is designed so another developer can clone the repository, install
the required Python dependencies, configure the database connection, and run
the analysis pipeline.

A typical setup is:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/perezamp15-hue/data510-capstone.git
cd data510-capstone

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt
